messages.author: 99f070a3a9d52cbf
messages.subject: Covariances and Regressions don't match
parts:
Hi,
I'm really confused right now and can't figure out what I'm doing wrong. So I have a model like this:

model <- "
# bifactor
A =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + ... + x90
A1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 ...
A2 =~ x10 + x11 + x12 ...
A3 =~ x19 + x20 + x21 ...
...
A9 =~ ... + x88 + x89 + x90

# criteria
B =~ b1 + b2 + b3 + ... + b10
C =~ c1 + c2 + c3 + ... + c9
D =~ d1 + d2 + d3 + ... + d9
"
Bascially, A and B are two variables that are correlated pretty strongly. C and D are two variables that are expected to be related differently to A and B, so for example A~~C > B~~C and A~~D < B~~D. Thus, I fit the model (model.fit <- cfa(model, data, std.lv = T)) and then check the correlations via inspect(model.fit, "cor.lv"). They are as follows:
A~~C = .130, B~~C = .185, A~~D = .580, B~~D = .744. So far so good.

Now I am also interested in the variance explained in C and D by A and B, respectively. So for each C and D, I estimate three seperate models: one with A, one with B and one with both A and B as predictors. I also let the specific factors of the bifactor model covary with the criterion. So for example, a regression model would look as follows:

reg.model <- "
# bifactor
A =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + ... + x90
A1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 ...
A2 =~ x10 + x11 + x12 ...
A3 =~ x19 + x20 + x21 ...
...
A9 =~ ... + x88 + x89 + x90

# criteria
B =~ b1 + b2 + b3 + ... + b10
C =~ c1 + c2 + c3 + ... + c9

# regression
C ~ A

# allowed covariances
C ~ B + A1 + A2 + A3 + ... + A9
"
Now, the betas look like this:
C ~ A beta = .293, R² = .079
C ~ B beta = .259, R² = .062

Shouldn't the correlation (i.e., the standardized covariance from the first model) and the beta be the same in the simple regression? And how is it possible, that the beta of C~B is smaller than the correlation C~~B?

I am really confused and hope somebody can shed a light here? Thanks so much in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Covariances and Regressions don't match
parts: Shouldn't the correlation (i.e., the standardized covariance from the first model) and the beta be the same in the simple regression?
I would expect so, but your syntax suggests you are running multiple regression:

# regression
C ~ A

# allowed covariances
C ~ B + A1 + A2 + A3 + ... + A9

The operator on the last line should be ~~ for covariance.  Also, if you are allowing B to covary with both the predictor (A) and outcome (C), I think that might lead to an identification issue, which could make results look different if the optimizer thinks it found a unique solution.  But I might be misremembering whether that makes a model nonrecursive.

messages.author: 99f070a3a9d52cbf
messages.subject: Re: Covariances and Regressions don't match
parts:
Oh good catch! Sorry, I guess that was a typo... In my script there is a double tilde, so I did specify a covariance.
I think I found my mistake though: in the one model, I had fixed the loadings of the first indicators to 1, but not in the other one... After removing those constraints, the regression and correlation coefficients match. Thanks for looking into this anyway!
